review_basis.method: Independent needs-to-understand review against each step's concept context and blocked_future_concepts. Reviewed all lesson and remediation text, including headings, ledes, visual labels, accessible descriptions, captions, media bridges and recap previews. Sampled interaction prompts, options/items/tasks and associated feedback across every tile. Did not consult generator reasoning, prior evaluator claims or deterministic gate reports; did not rerun gates.

coverage.sample_selection: Distributed across every tile, with additional coverage for multi-concept scripting, artifact publication and workload identity tiles; includes choice, classify and table_select interactions.

findings_summary: No reviewed text or sampled interaction requires understanding a blocked future concept.
Multi-concept tiles introduce each concept in its own sequence. Shared recaps summarize already introduced material rather than making earlier steps depend on later concepts.
The Pod/controller distinction does not require understanding deployment-controller operation. The supplied status, events and intended-container evidence are sufficient for this tile.
Artifact attestation permissions, including id-token: write, are explicitly part of the artifact glossary facts. This lesson does not require understanding the later AWS OIDC federation trust model.

The identity lessons mention temporary credentials before the detailed STS lesson, but their association and trust checks do not require understanding STS credential composition or session-policy evaluation. Those details are introduced in the STS sequence itself.
Event matching is explained only as selection, separately from the target's authorization model. No later operational event-routing, Lambda operation or failed-delivery handling knowledge is needed.
The two registered datasets provide self-contained fictional restart and review-handoff evidence. Neither requires later incident-recovery or delivery-pipeline implementation knowledge.
Up-next titles are passing previews, not prerequisite knowledge or assessment requirements.
